title: ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search
content:
Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence
  [Submitted on 11 Sep 2026]
    Title:ZGCM-1: A Fully Open and Extremely Efficient Foundation Model for Math and Agentic Search
View PDF HTML (experimental)
            Abstract:In this work, we present ZGCM-1, a fully open 7B dense foundation model trained from scratch with extreme data, system, and algorithmic efficiency. ZGCM-1 is founded on a core premise: compact models cannot passively memorize the open web, but can overcome parametric capacity limits by coupling deliberate internal thinking with active external tool use. To support this paradigm across a 256K context, we develop an end-to-end, high-efficiency open training recipe: Architecture & System Co-design: interleaved gated sliding-window and full attention, and a stable FP8 Muon optimizer; Progressive Curriculum & MDP Mid-Training: context scaling across 16K, 64K, and 256K, and the reformulation of interaction traces into Markov Decision Processes. Furthermore, we establish an AI-native R&D workflow where agent swarms autonomously manage cluster operations, data curation, and rapid diagnostic evaluation. Extensive evaluations show that ZGCM-1-7B is competitive across 7B model family on general benchmarks. On several challenging mathematical reasoning and agentic search suites, it remains competitive with frontier models orders of magnitude larger, such as Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.1. We also show that our pre-training design offers a ~4.2x efficiency improvement in 16K pre-training time-to-loss. Across the full development lifecycle, we distill eight actionable empirical findings-spanning architectural scaling, SFT quality pruning, long-context generalization, and agentic co-training dynamics. To facilitate community research, we open-source model weights from the pre-training, mid-training, and post-training stages, intermediate checkpoints, training code, per-stage data and data recipes, and W&B logs.

report.summary: ZGCM-1 is a fully open 7B model that pairs internal reasoning with external tool use, rivaling far larger frontier models on math and agentic search.
report.background: The AI field has largely chased scale, with frontier systems exceeding 200B parameters. ZGCM-1 argues the opposite: a compact dense model can overcome parametric limits by thinking deliberately and calling tools instead of memorizing the open web. It sits at the intersection of three trends — fully open model releases, long-context training (256K tokens), and agentic search benchmarks that reward retrieval, code execution, and verification. Training efficiency is also central: FP8 precision, the Muon optimizer, and system-architecture co-design aim to cut compute. The paper's 'AI-native R&D' angle — agent swarms running clusters, curating data, and evaluating runs — suggests how future models may be built with less human labor.
key_points: Fully open release: ZGCM-1 provides pre-training, mid-training, and post-training weights, intermediate checkpoints, training code, per-stage data recipes, and W&B logs. This is unusually complete transparency for a foundation model, letting researchers reproduce or audit every development stage rather than only fine-tuning a black-box release.

Efficient architecture and training: It combines interleaved gated sliding-window and full attention with a stable FP8 Muon optimizer, scaling context from 16K to 64K to 256K. The design reportedly yields about a 4.2x improvement in 16K pre-training time-to-loss, a meaningful reduction in compute cost for a from-scratch dense model.

Tool use as a core paradigm: The model is trained to couple internal thinking with active external tool use, with interaction traces reformulated as Markov Decision Processes during mid-training. This shifts agentic behavior from a post-hoc fine-tuning step into the pre-training and mid-training pipeline.

AI-native R&D workflow: Agent swarms autonomously manage cluster operations, data curation, and rapid diagnostic evaluation. This meta-level automation is presented as part of the recipe, not just the product, hinting at how model development itself may be increasingly agent-driven.

Competitive results against giants: On general 7B benchmarks ZGCM-1 is competitive within its size class, and on challenging math reasoning and agentic search suites it remains competitive with Qwen3-235B-A22B and GLM-5.1. The paper distills eight empirical findings across scaling, SFT pruning, long-context generalization, and co-training dynamics.
report.impact: For the AI industry, ZGCM-1 challenges the assumption that only massive frontier models can handle hard math and agentic search. If its claims hold, small dense models with long context and tool use become a viable, cheaper path — and full open releases raise the reproducibility bar. For developers, the published weights, checkpoints, and data recipes lower the barrier to training or fine-tuning specialized agents, while a 7B model with 256K context is far easier to serve locally or on modest GPUs. Regular users could see faster, cheaper, more private assistants that search, calculate, and verify rather than hallucinate. The main caveats: benchmark claims need independent verification, and a 7B model's factual breadth still lags larger systems.
report.tools: Follow the official release for weights and checkpoints on Hugging Face Hub, plus training code, data recipes, and W&B logs linked from the paper. For serving long-context 7B models, watch vLLM and SGLang. For agentic search replication, see Search-R1, ReTool, and open deep-research projects. Muon optimizer and FP8 training implementations are worth tracking for efficient pre-training reproduction. DagsHub or similar tools can help manage the open data pipeline.
